hypotheses.claim: Notification scoping is by JWT subject, not role: the 3 unguarded endpoints cannot read another user's notifications.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: markRead's fallback findFirst leaks existence of another user's notification, or AuthGuard is bypassable without @Roles so an unauthenticated caller reaches list().
hypotheses.altCheck: read notifications.controller.ts:14-40 — class-level @UseGuards(AuthGuard, RoleGuard); every service call passes user.user_id and every where-clause carries recipientUserId (notification.service.ts:92,117,122,128). Static read says scoped; only a two-token walk settles it.

hypotheses.claim: No admin screen anywhere consumes GET /api/audit-trail/tickets/:id — an Operations Head cannot reach the audit trail from the product.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: A ticket-detail drawer calls it under a different name (history, timeline, activity) or via a generic fetch helper the grep missed.
hypotheses.altCheck: grep -rniE 'audit-trail|auditTrail|/notifications' apps/admin/src = 0 hits; skeleton.md 'admin UI files' and 'admin api client calls' sections are both empty.

hypotheses.claim: device_tokens is empty in every environment — no client registers a token, so a push adapter would have nothing to send to.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: A native/Expo config plugin or an admin-side registration writes tokens outside apps/mobile/src.
hypotheses.altCheck: grep -rniE 'device-token|deviceToken|expo-notifications|firebase|fcm|apns' apps/mobile/src apps/mobile/package.json = 0 hits beyond unrelated array .push().

hypotheses.claim: Mark-read persists: the SE's read state survives app reload, so the list stays usable across a full day of stops.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: markRead's swallowed catch (NotificationsScreen.tsx:52) hides a failing write, so the row re-appears unread after reload while the UI showed it read.
hypotheses.altCheck: read NotificationsScreen.tsx:47-60 — the catch is empty and load(filter) refetches immediately after, which would surface a failed write; still needs a real save-and-reload.

hypotheses.claim: Audit rows carry acted_as_role from real delegated sessions, not just nulls — the write path is exercised, so only the read side is missing.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: Most audited controllers hardcode actedAsRole: null instead of using auditActor(), so the column is null even during a genuine CSM-in-ZM-scope session and the whole capability is a facade.
hypotheses.altCheck: grep actedAsRole across apps/backend/src — cross-zone.controller.ts:113, devices.controller.ts:131, engineers.controller.ts:254, leave-request.controller.ts:69,85,103 all pass literal null; acting-context.ts:30 is the only place a non-null is derived. A real acted-as session must be walked to see which path wins.
